newsitem.title: USA: U.S. aluminum premiums firmer on weaker imports.
newsitem.headline: U.S. aluminum premiums firmer on weaker imports.

text.p: The U.S. Midwest aluminum premium firmed this week as the market continues to feel the pinch of fewer imports from Russia, dealers said.
The Midwest premium is 4.75-5.25 cents over the LME cash price, up 0.50 cents from last week.
"People are still getting used to the lack of imports from Russia," one New York merchant said. "The lead times at the producers are coming out. If you want guaranteed delivery, you have to pay up."
Premiums typically need to rise to 6.00-7.00 cents to profitably import metal from Russia, dealers say.
